content.text: The text reviews diseases of the mouth, tongue, tonsils, pharynx, oesophagus, and stomach. It describes gangrenous stomatitis, mercurial stomatitis, congenital tongue abnormalities, macroglossia, glossitis, tongue ulcers, tonsillitis, acute and chronic pharyngitis, oesophagitis, strictures, cancer, paralysis, diverticula, and functional dyspepsia. Across conditions it emphasizes causes, pathological changes, symptoms, differential diagnosis, prognosis, complications, and historical treatments. Severe disorders may cause obstruction, hemorrhage, gangrene, aspiration, malnutrition, or death. Management historically includes local cleansing, cautery, diet modification, supportive nutrition, medicinal agents, dilation, drainage, and surgery. Functional dyspepsia is linked to nervous, dietary, constitutional, hepatic, intestinal, and lifestyle factors, with hygiene and appropriate diet considered central. Daniel moved to the office.
